Former Apple design chief Jony Ive has long described his long-term vision for iPhone design as "a slab of glass." The outside world believes Apple is still pursuing this goal even after Ive's departure, and Liquid Glass is the software preparation this company has made for the new hardware.

We've already seen numerous reports discussing how the 20th anniversary edition iPhone could bring us closer to Apple's vision, and the latest report may add another piece to this puzzle...

What we're expecting

There were originally some who thought Apple might launch a standalone 20th anniversary special edition iPhone, but more recent reports suggest it will be the iPhone 19 Pro that gets all the "glass unibody" design elements. Making things even more complicated, some believe Apple will skip the iPhone 19 name to mark this milestone and go straight with iPhone 20 Pro.

There's still quite some time before the launch, so these reports are largely speculative, but the most important design feature is expected to be a display that curves on all four sides, making the device appear completely bezel-less.

It looks like the year Apple can finally embed the Face ID module under the display is nearly here, while the front camera and speaker are also expected to be placed beneath the screen.

All of the above combined could create a very convincing "slab of glass" effect.

Glass back

Leaker Fixed Focus Digital now says there's another design element: a return to a glass back, rather than the aluminium used in recent models.

A glass back would admittedly make the device more fragile, but it would certainly help achieve that "slab of glass" look. Do you think this trade-off is worth it for a strikingly futuristic design? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
